title: New potato, cauliflower and walnut pesto pasta

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Every ingredient is a whole food or a basic cupboard item, such as walnuts, cheese, olive oil, pasta and fresh vegetables, with no jars or packet mixes.

supermarket.reason: New potatoes, cauliflower, penne, walnuts, vegetarian hard cheese, lemon and parsley are all everyday Tesco items at normal prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only one pan, a knife and board, a grater and a bowl, and a hand-chopped pesto is within reach of a beginner.

works.reason: Potatoes get a head start before the pasta and florets, the quantities suit four, and the pesto is loosened with pasta water, so it should come out well balanced.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes of active work is believable because the pesto is made while the pan boils, and twenty minutes covers 8 minutes for the potatoes plus about 10 for the pasta.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed item, including salt, pepper, lemon and parsley, appears in the steps, penne is a fair name for dried pasta, and nothing unlisted is used.

seasonal_feel.reason: Mid-April new potatoes lead the dish in the classic pasta, potato and pesto style, with spring parsley and cauliflower alongside.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British English with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a filling family lunch with vegetables, nuts and cheese alongside the starch, not just plain refined carbohydrate.
